correctness.rationale: For SSEP with rate one per undirected bond, the Bessel heat-kernel mean is exact. Pair covariances solve a two-particle exclusion evolution with nonpositive source at adjacent indices and zero initial data, establishing Var(J0(t))<=m(t). Combined with m(t)~sqrt(t/pi), J0(y^2 u)/y converges in probability. Alternating-renewal rewards have normalized density Psi_s/M. Dominated convergence for ages above epsilon y^2 and a second-moment bound below it yield sharp P(Y>y),P(Y<-y) with constants; alpha<2 closes the short-age estimate. Strict monotonicity of expected H(bU), with alpha>3/2 ensuring E[U^(3/2)]<infinity, gives the unique zero-mean cutoff. Exact limits and finite-vs-infinite moments follow. Python verify.py passed 81 finite numerical checks, not relied upon as proof.

value.rationale: The 2020 dichotomous SSEP literature motivates zero-current nonequilibrium states, while the 2022 Pareto-reset SSEP paper motivates nontrivial stationary current fluctuations and moment transitions. The new exact calibration creates zero mean but two different tail exponents with infinite variance; it gives sharp coefficients for an interacting system using a nontrivial covariance bound. This separates mean-balance from fluctuation-balance under physically natural heterogeneous renewal control, and is not a narrow arbitrary numerical slice.
